query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a trace microalloying element (e.g., boron) that segregates to lamellar interfaces can enhance interfacial cohesion, reducing microcrack nucleation and propagation while also providing additional dislocation pinning to boost strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy (AlCoCrFeNi2.1) produced via suction casting, heavy cold-rolling, and annealing to form dual-phase lamellar colonies with internal boundaries that are prone to microcrack initiation under room‐temperature tensile deformation.
generation.intervention: Add a controlled, small amount (on the order of ~0.5 at%) of boron during alloy melting so that, during subsequent thermo‐mechanical processing, boron segregates preferentially to the lamellar interfaces.
generation.conditions: Maintain the same processing route (84–86% cold-rolling and annealing at an optimal temperature such as 700 °C for 1 h) while carefully controlling boron content to avoid forming brittle boride phases.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced chemical segregation at internal lamellar boundaries, leading to improved cohesion and modified precipitate/dislocation interactions in the vicinity of the interfaces.
generation.mechanism: Boron segregation at the lamellar interfaces strengthens the interfacial bonding, postponing microcrack initiation and reducing crack coalescence. Concurrently, its interaction with dislocations provides effective pinning, which improves yield strength. This dual effect is expected to lead to a better balance between strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unmodified DPHL baseline, the boron-added alloy is predicted to exhibit higher yield strength and increased uniform elongation (ductility) as microcrack formation is delayed and dislocation motion is effectively moderated.
generation.baseline: The unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy with inherited lamellar architecture that shows a limited tensile ductility because of microcrack initiation at internal boundaries.
generation.boundary: Effective only if the boron content remains within a narrow trace range; excessive boron could form brittle intermetallics rather than segregate beneficially. The effect depends on processing conditions that promote interfacial segregation.
generation.uncertainty: The precise amount of boron required to achieve optimal segregation without forming unwanted phases and the quantitative improvement in strength and ductility remain to be determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA samples: one with the trace boron addition and one without (control). Ensure both sets undergo identical suction-casting, heavy cold-rolling, and annealing (e.g., at 700 °C for 1 h).
measurements: Tensile testing at room temperature to measure yield strength and uniform elongation.
Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) to verify boron segregation at the lamellar interfaces.
Fractography to assess microcrack initiation and propagation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in both yield strength and ductility (or show deteriorated properties due to brittle intermetallic formation) compared to the control, the hypothesis is falsified.

top3.builds_on: The paper shows that the internal interfaces in the lamellar microstructure are critical sites for damage initiation; improving interfacial cohesion via nanoscale phenomena is a logical extension.
top3.what_is_new: This hypothesis proposes a single-composition intervention (controlled minor Boron doping) aimed primarily at strengthening lamellar boundaries, rather than adjusting the bulk phase precipitate structure or processing conditions as in the paper.

fields.hypothesis: Minor doping with an interfacial segregant (e.g., ~0.1–0.5 at.% Boron) will improve both yield strength and room‐temperature tensile ductility by strengthening the internal lamellar boundaries, thereby delaying microcrack nucleation and promoting more homogeneous plasticity.
fields.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy (Al0.7CoCrFeNi) with dual-phase lamellar colonies (fcc/L12 and B2/bcc) produced by conventional thermo-mechanical processing, which exhibits numerous inter-lamellar boundaries that act as sites for microcrack initiation.
fields.intervention: Introduce a minor doping addition of Boron during melting to promote boundary segregation.
fields.conditions: The alloy is prepared by conventional melting-mixing with a controlled addition of ~0.1–0.5 at.% Boron; standard homogenization, rolling, and annealing treatments are otherwise maintained.
fields.structural_mediator: Boron segregation at the internal fcc–B2 (or fcc–bcc) interfaces.
fields.mechanism: Boron is known to segregate preferentially to grain or interphase boundaries where it can reduce the boundary energy and improve cohesion. This segregation reinforces the lamellar interfaces, thereby reducing stress concentrations and mitigating early microcrack initiation during deformation. In addition, stronger interfaces may slightly contribute to additional barriers for dislocation motion (via a pinning effect), resulting in modest strengthening without compromising ductility.
fields.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unmodified alloy, the doped alloy is expected to exhibit a higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength while also showing increased elongation before failure. The improvement in ductility is predicted to be significant if microcrack nucleation is suppressed, though the precise percent increase is uncertain.
fields.baseline: Conventional eutectic HEA in the as-processed lamellar condition that fails at room temperature via microcracking initiated at weak interphase boundaries.
fields.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected to operate only if the Boron addition is small enough not to form detrimental boride phases; excessive doping may lead to the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds. The processing parameters should permit sufficient segregation without extra annealing steps.
fields.uncertainty: The optimal Boron level and exact quantitative improvement need to be established experimentally, and small changes in local chemistry might affect phase stability.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Boron-doped alloy does not show statistically significant improvements in both strength and ductility compared to the baseline (or shows formation of undesirable brittle phases), the hypothesis is falsified.

top3.builds_on: the detailed observation of a nano-lamellar eutectoid-like microstructure in Al0.3CoFeNi (PMC7075928) and the known benefits of refined microstructural spacing (Hall–Petch effect) with coherent boundaries.
top3.what_is_new: It proposes a modified post-annealing cooling route – a rapid quench – specifically to freeze in the beneficial ordering and spinodal decomposition structures, a single intervention not explored in the paper.

fields.hypothesis: A rapid quench immediately after the 600 °C, 50‐hr annealing (CRSA600) can freeze in a more refined and coherent nano‐lamellar microstructure with improved interfacial integrity, thereby reducing microcrack‐nucleation sites and simultaneously enhancing both strength and room-temperature ductility.
fields.material_initial_state: Al0.3CoFeNi HEA processed via the conventional CRSA600 route, which produces a nano‐lamellar eutectoid-like microstructure with alternating FCC + L12 and BCC + B2 lamellae, but with interlamellar boundaries that can serve as microcrack initiation sites.
fields.intervention: Immediately after the 50‐hr annealing at 600 °C, subject the alloy to a rapid quench (e.g., water or oil quench) to room temperature rather than a slow cool.
fields.conditions: The rapid quench must be initiated directly upon completion of the 600 °C annealing stage; the alloy composition and thermal history prior to quenching should follow the CRSA600 schedule. The quenching media and cooling rate must be chosen to avoid thermal shock that could induce macro‐cracking.
fields.structural_mediator: A finer, less coarsened nano-lamellar structure with preserved ordering and reduced interfacial relaxation that minimizes the formation of weak, diffusely bonded internal boundaries.
fields.mechanism: Rapid quenching will freeze the existing spinodal and ordering microstructures before any coarsening or interface relaxation can occur. This ‘freezing in’ limits the thermal activation that might otherwise allow for increased inhomogeneity at the lamellar interfaces. As a result, the distance between strong ordered domains is maintained at a fine scale, which, via an improved Hall–Petch effect, increases yield strength, while the improved interfacial bonding suppresses premature microcracking and enhances ductility. This builds on the demonstration of a hierarchical eutectoid-like lamellar structure in Al0.3CoFeNi (PMC7075928::web::003–016) and applies a modified cooling pathway to preserve its optimum features.
fields.predicted_outcome: Compared with a conventionally slow-cooled CRSA600 sample, the rapidly quenched samples are expected to show moderate (estimated ~10–20%) increases in yield and ultimate tensile strengths and improved ductility (fewer microcracks and increased elongation) at room temperature.
fields.baseline: A CRSA600 sample cooled at a controlled, slow rate after annealing, resulting in a nano-lamellar structure that may be prone to localized interfacial weakness and microcrack initiation.
fields.boundary: This approach is applicable only if the quenching is sufficiently rapid to freeze in the fine microstructure without inducing additional thermal stresses that cause macro-cracks; it must also be compatible with the alloy’s thermal expansion properties.
fields.uncertainty: The exact quantitative gains in strength and ductility are uncertain and may depend on the quench rate achieved; excessive quenching might risk additional thermal stresses.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of Al0.3CoFeNi specimens following the CRSA600 processing route. One group is cooled slowly at conventional rates; the other group is subjected to immediate rapid quenching. Perform identical room-temperature tensile tests and microstructural evaluations (via SEM/TEM) on both groups.
measurements: Lamellar spacing and interfacial quality via high-resolution microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the rapidly quenched samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements (e.g., >10% increase in both strength and ductility) or show evidence of additional quench-induced defects, the hypothesis is falsified.
